title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 34 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: budget, policy & acquisition reform and drones & air autonomy.

stories.h: Senate Backs Bigger Space Force, but Trims Pentagon Plans
stories.what: The Senate Appropriations Committee approved a plan to raise investment in the Space Force by 73 percent over 2026—but its bid falls well short of the Pentagon's request. Under the plan, the Space Force would get $54.7 billion—up from $31.6 billion this year.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: Senate grills acting Navy secretary on Iran war costs, extended deployments
stories.what: Democrats in particular bristled at Hung Cao’s characterization of unsuccessful suicide attempts as “mitigations.”
stories.you: The Navy is short of ships and is turning to cheaper unmanned boats, which opens the door to new builders.

stories.h: OpenAI gives NATO access to most advanced cybersecurity AI
stories.what: NATO operators this month built and deployed AI agents in an exercise, with help from OpenAI.
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

stories.h: Lockheed says its Valkyrie laser downs cruise missile
stories.what: A Lockheed Martin high-energy laser has destroyed a surrogate cruise missile target for the first time, a company executive said, months after the U.S. Army said it no longer planned to put the same weapon into service.
stories.you: Weapons stockpiles are short, so anyone who can make missiles and rocket motors faster and cheaper has buyers.

stories.h: Lockheed gets $93M to help military mechanics fix F-35s faster
stories.what: The U.S. Navy is paying Lockheed Martin $93.2 million to help military repair shops fix more F-35 parts themselves. The money buys new test equipment, software updates and extra capacity to repair the jet’s ejection seats.
stories.you: The big incumbents are growing too. Watch where they partner with or buy startups rather than compete.

watch.h: Stopgap funding expires: FY27 appropriations or another CR
watch.why: December 11. Decides whether DAWG's $54.6B and Golden Dome's growth become real money.

idea.why: An autonomous interceptor under $5k for Shahed-class and FPV drones. Ukraine proved the concept, and Japan, the Gulf and US bases are buying. The cost-exchange crisis is acute.
